Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-worlds -b feature/freemc-worlds main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-worlds`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env`. Do all work there.

CONTEXT: The free Minecraft product (one free Docker-based Minecraft server per account on "freemc-host", a real `Server` row with `hostname="freemc-host"`) currently has ONE shared `/data` world folder per account, and a single "preset" concept covering 12 flat options (Vanilla/Creative/Hardcore/Peaceful — properties-only — plus SkyBlock/Prison/Towny/Parkour/Anarchy/Lifesteal SMP/Missile Wars/Survival Games — plugin-based). Switching between them all shares the SAME world files, which just caused a real production incident: a customer switched from SkyBlock back to Vanilla and their world became unbootable, because Paper/IridiumSkyblock had rewritten the shared world's dimension registry data in a format plain vanilla couldn't parse. Read `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` in full (especially `applyFreeMinecraftPreset` and `recreatePresetContainer`) and `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` (especially `FREEMC_PRESETS`) before doing anything — these establish every pattern you must follow: `withServerSsh`/`exec` for SSH, `shellQuote` for every value in a remote command, the mandatory `sleep(15000)` + `docker inspect` health-check-then-rollback pattern after any `docker run`, `rconPasswordFor`/`sendRcon` for RCON, `FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION = "26.1.2"` pinned on every plugins-kind container.

YOUR TASK — split the current flat "preset" concept into two independent axes, each with isolated persistent storage, per this exact product decision (already agreed with the user, matches a UI redesign happening in parallel by another agent — you must produce the exact action names/shapes below since that other agent is building against this contract sight-unseen):

## 1. GAME MODE vs GAME TYPE
- **GAME TYPE** = which world/game-experience: `vanilla` (plain, no plugins), `skyblock`, `prison`, `towny`, `parkour`, `anarchy`, `lifesteal`, `missilewars`, `survivalgames` — 9 total. Each GAME TYPE gets its own ISOLATED, persistent saved world — switching types never touches another type's world data again (this directly fixes the production incident above).
- **GAME MODE** = `survival` / `hardcore` / `creative` / `peaceful` — a lightweight property overlay (gamemode/hardcore/difficulty in server.properties) applied WITHIN whichever GAME TYPE is currently active, via RCON + a restart of the SAME container — no world-switch, no recreate. This does NOT get its own isolated world; it's just settings on top of the currently-active type's world.
- Restructure `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`: rename/reshape `FREEMC_PRESETS` into `FREEMC_GAME_TYPES` (9 entries, drop `hardcore`/`creative`/`peaceful` as standalone type entries — those become modes now, not types) and a new `FREEMC_GAME_MODES` (4 entries: `survival`, `hardcore`, `creative`, `peaceful`, each just `{ label, description, properties: {gamemode, hardcore, difficulty} }`). Keep every existing field on game-type entries (`kind`, `type`, `env`, `heroImage`, `setupNote`) — game types still have a base `properties` object too (their own default gamemode/difficulty when no mode override has been applied yet).

## 2. Per-type isolated world storage — use itzg's `LEVEL` env var
itzg/docker-minecraft-server supports `-e LEVEL=<name>` to set the world-folder name (default is `world`) — everything still lives under the same `/data` volume mount, just in a differently-named subfolder, so you do NOT need to change the volume mount strategy, only add this one env var. Set `LEVEL` to the sanitized game-type key (e.g. `LEVEL=skyblock`) on every container launch in `recreatePresetContainer` (or its replacement). This means: switching game types now means recreating the container with the SAME data volume but a DIFFERENT `LEVEL`, so each type's Minecraft naturally creates/reuses its own `<LEVEL>`, `<LEVEL>_nether`, `<LEVEL>_the_end` folders and never touches another type's — confirm this is really how `LEVEL` behaves by testing it live (see verification section) before assuming.

## 3. Schema addition
Add a new Prisma model to track per-account saved worlds for the UI (list/rename/last-played), e.g.:
```prisma
model FreeMinecraftWorld {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  serverId   String
  server     FreeMinecraftServer @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  gameType   String   // FREEMC_GAME_TYPES key
  label      String?  // customer-chosen display name, defaults to the type's own label
  lastPlayedAt DateTime?
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
  @@unique([serverId, gameType])
}
```
Add the inverse relation on `FreeMinecraftServer`. Also add `activeGameType String @default("vanilla")` and `activeGameMode String @default("survival")` fields to `FreeMinecraftServer` (replacing the old flat `preset` field's role — check every existing read of `row.preset` across the codebase via `grep -rn "\.preset\b" lib/ components/ app/` and update each call site; do NOT leave `preset` half-migrated). Do NOT run `prisma db push` yourself against any real database — schema changes ship via the normal deploy pipeline (staging db push happens when I integrate this), just write the schema.

## 4. Server actions — `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts`, `"use server"` — EXACT names/shapes required (the parallel UI agent is coding against these):
- `listFreeMinecraftWorlds(): Promise<{ ok: true; worlds: { gameType: string; label: string; lastPlayedAt: string | null; isActive: boolean }[] } | { ok: false; error: string }>` — one row per `FreeMinecraftWorld` that exists for the caller's server (a world only "exists" once that game type has actually been applied at least once — don't pre-create all 9).
- `switchFreeMinecraftGameType(prev: unknown, formData: FormData): Promise<{ error?: string }>` — formData has `gameType`. Recreates the container with the target type's `LEVEL`/env, same rollback-on-failure discipline as the current `applyFreeMinecraftPreset`. Upserts a `FreeMinecraftWorld` row (creating one on first-ever visit to that type), updates `lastPlayedAt`, updates `FreeMinecraftServer.activeGameType`.
- `applyFreeMinecraftGameMode(prev: unknown, formData: FormData): Promise<{ error?: string }>` — formData has `gameMode`. Applies the mode's properties via RCON + restart (NOT a recreate) to the currently-active container, updates `FreeMinecraftServer.activeGameMode`.
- `renameFreeMinecraftWorld(prev: unknown, formData: FormData): Promise<{ error?: string }>` — formData has `gameType`, `label` (trim, cap ~40 chars).
- `deleteFreeMinecraftWorld(prev: unknown, formData: FormData): Promise<{ error?: string }>` — formData has `gameType`. Refuse (clear error) if `gameType === activeGameType` — the currently-active world can't be deleted out from under itself, must switch away first. On the freemc-host, this means removing that `<LEVEL>*` world folder set from the data volume (careful: exact folder names, don't `rm -rf` the whole `/data` dir) and deleting the `FreeMinecraftWorld` row.

Keep `checkRateLimit` + `requireUser` + ownership checks on every mutating action, matching the existing file's conventions exactly.

## 5. Update the existing create/apply/subdomain-change/rollback code paths in `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` to use the new two-axis model instead of the old flat preset. `createFreeMinecraftServer` should default to `gameType=vanilla, gameMode=survival`. Keep backward compatibility for the ALREADY-DEPLOYED database: do not assume every existing `FreeMinecraftServer` row has been migrated — if you drop the old `preset` column entirely, make sure there's no code path left reading it (grep exhaustively, see above).

## 6. LIVE VERIFICATION (mandatory, this is exactly the kind of thing that looks right in code and silently isn't) — against the real freemc-host, `db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`:
- Boot a container with `LEVEL=testmodeA`, then a SECOND container (different container name so you don't clobber anything real, e.g. `mc-worldtest`) with `LEVEL=testmodeB` on the SAME data volume path, confirm via `docker exec ... ls /data` that BOTH `testmodeA*` and `testmodeB*` folder sets exist independently and neither was touched by the other's boot.
- Confirm a `docker run` with `LEVEL=skyblock` on a Paper/plugins-kind container actually creates `skyblock`, `skyblock_nether`, `skyblock_the_end` (not just `world*`) — plugins like IridiumSkyblock create ADDITIONAL custom-named dimensions on top of the base ones (you saw `iridiumskyblock`/`iridiumskyblock_nether`/`iridiumskyblock_the_end` in earlier testing) — confirm those also respect the LEVEL-based naming and don't collide with a different type's custom dimensions.
- Confirm switching game TYPE while staying on the same game MODE doesn't lose the mode setting, and switching MODE while staying on the same TYPE doesn't disturb that type's other saved world data.
- Clean up all test containers/data before finishing.

## Constraints
- Do NOT edit `components/customer/freemc/*.tsx` (the parallel agent owns those) or `FreeMcDashboard.tsx`.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` must both pass clean.
- Commit explicitly named files (never `-A`). Don't merge to main, don't delete your worktree, don't run `prisma db push` against any real database.

Report back: the final `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts` action signatures (confirm they match exactly what's specified above — if you had to deviate, say so loudly and why), the schema diff, how the old flat `preset` field/reads were migrated, what you verified live and the results, and confirmation build/typecheck passed.

3	 * freemc-host — the free-tier equivalent of lib/game-control.ts, which speaks
4	 * to full Proxmox-VM game servers over SSH+tunnelled RCON. This is much
5	 * simpler: one SSH hop to the host, then `docker exec <container> ...` for
6	 * everything, using the CLI tools itzg/docker-minecraft-server already bundles
7	 * (rcon-cli, mc-monitor) instead of a hand-rolled RCON protocol client.
8	 *
9	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from both lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
10	 * and, in future, a worker sweep, same reasoning as lib/game-control.ts.
11	 */
12	import { scryptSync } from "node:crypto";
13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
15	
16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}
28	
29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}
33	
34	export type ServerStatus = {
35	  running: boolean;
36	  players: { online: number; max: number } | null;
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
52	    return { running: false, players: null };
53	  }
54	  const status = await dockerExec(
55	    conn,
56	    containerName,
57	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
58	    10_000,
59	  );
60	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
61	  try {
62	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);
63	    const p = parsed?.server_info?.players;
64	    if (typeof p?.online === "number" && typeof p?.max === "number") {
65	      return { running: true, players: { online: p.online, max: p.max } };
66	    }
67	  } catch {
68	    /* fall through */
69	  }
70	  return { running: true, players: null };
71	}
72	
73	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
74	
75	/** One RCON round-trip via the bundled rcon-cli — see lib/game-control.ts's
76	 *  validateRconCommand for the same input sanitation used on the paid path. */
77	export async function sendRcon(
78	  conn: Client,
79	  containerName: string,
80	  ownerId: string,
81	  command: string,
82	): Promise<RconResult> {
83	  const password = rconPasswordFor(ownerId);
84	  const r = await dockerExec(
85	    conn,
86	    containerName,
87	    `env RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(password)} rcon-cli ${shellQuote(command)}`,
88	    12_000,
89	  );
90	  if (r.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: r.stderr.trim() || "RCON command failed." };
91	  return { ok: true, response: r.stdout.trim() };
92	}
93	
94	export type PlayerInfo = { name: string };
95	
96	/** Parses rcon-cli's `list` response: "There are N of a max of M players online: a, b, c" */
97	export async function getFreeServerPlayers(
98	  conn: Client,
99	  containerName: string,
100	  ownerId: string,
101	): Promise<{ ok: true; players: PlayerInfo[] } | { ok: false; error: string }> {
102	  const r = await sendRcon(conn, containerName, ownerId, "list");
103	  if (!r.ok) return r;
104	  const colonIdx = r.response.indexOf(":");
105	  if (colonIdx === -1) return { ok: true, players: [] };
106	  const names = r.response
107	    .slice(colonIdx + 1)
108	    .split(",")
109	    .map((s) => s.trim())
110	    .filter(Boolean);
111	  return { ok: true, players: names.map((name) => ({ name })) };
112	}

114	/** Reads /data/server.properties into a plain key->value map. */
115	export async function readServerProperties(
116	  conn: Client,
117	  containerName: string,
118	): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
119	  const r = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, "cat /data/server.properties", 10_000);
120	  if (r.code !== 0) return {};
121	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
122	  for (const line of r.stdout.split("\n")) {
123	    if (!line || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
124	    const i = line.indexOf("=");
125	    if (i === -1) continue;
126	    out[line.slice(0, i).trim()] = line.slice(i + 1).trim();
127	  }
128	  return out;
129	}

131	/**
132	 * Writes a set of server.properties keys in place (sed-style line replace,
133	 * appending any key not already present) and restarts the container so the
134	 * itzg entrypoint's normal boot sequence picks the new values up — the image
135	 * only reads server.properties at startup (confirmed against the Minecraft
136	 * wiki: none of gamemode/motd/max-players/etc. persist a live RCON change back
137	 * to the file), so a restart is the only fully-reliable way to apply anything
138	 * here. Keys with a real live RCON equivalent (difficulty, whitelist on/off)
139	 * are ALSO pushed live by the caller for instant effect — see FIELD_LIVE_CMD.
140	 */
141	export async function writeServerProperties(
142	  conn: Client,
143	  containerName: string,
144	  changes: Record<string, string>,
145	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
146	  const current = await readServerProperties(conn, containerName);
147	  const merged = { ...current, ...changes };
148	  const body = Object.entries(merged)
149	    .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`)
150	    .join("\n");
151	  const write = await execInput(
152	    conn,
153	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c 'cat > /data/server.properties'`,
154	    body + "\n",
155	    10_000,
156	  );
157	  if (write.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: write.stderr.trim() || "Could not write server.properties." };
158	  return { ok: true };
159	}

161	/** Given a MINECRAFT ConfigField key, the live RCON command to fire for
162	 *  instant effect (null = restart-only, no live equivalent) — see the
163	 *  research summary in the dashboard build: difficulty and whitelist on/off
164	 *  have real vanilla commands; gamemode's live command only affects players
165	 *  currently online (not new joiners), so it's listed as restart-only here to
166	 *  avoid a UI that claims "applied" while a reconnecting player gets the old
167	 *  value. MOTD and max-players have no vanilla live command at all. */
168	export function liveRconCommandFor(key: string, value: string): string | null {
169	  if (key === "difficulty") return `difficulty ${value}`;
170	  if (key === "white-list") return `whitelist ${value === "true" ? "on" : "off"}`;
171	  return null;
172	}

174	/** server.properties key -> itzg env var name, for the handful of keys the
175	 *  preset table actually sets. Only needed when RECREATING a container
176	 *  (kind:"plugins" presets) — a plain property-file write (kind:"properties")
177	 *  never goes through env vars at all. */
178	const PROPERTY_TO_ENV: Record<string, string> = {
179	  gamemode: "MODE",
180	  difficulty: "DIFFICULTY",
181	  pvp: "PVP",
182	  hardcore: "HARDCORE",
183	  motd: "MOTD",
184	  "max-players": "MAX_PLAYERS",
185	  "white-list": "ENABLE_WHITELIST",
186	  "view-distance": "VIEW_DISTANCE",
187	  "spawn-protection": "SPAWN_PROTECTION",
188	};

190	/** Translates a preset's `properties` map into the itzg env vars a fresh
191	 *  `docker run` needs to boot with those settings already applied. */
192	export function propertiesToEnv(properties: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string> {
193	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
194	  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(properties)) {
195	    const envKey = PROPERTY_TO_ENV[k];
196	    if (envKey) out[envKey] = v;
197	  }
198	  return out;
199	}

201	/**
202	 * Minecraft version every plugin-based preset pins to, instead of tracking
203	 * itzg's default `LATEST`. Found via live testing, not assumed: right after
204	 * Minecraft's newest calendar release ("26.2"), EssentialsX's latest
205	 * published build only declared support up to 26.1.2 — MODRINTH_PROJECTS
206	 * refused to download it at all, which killed the container seconds into its

Running `prisma generate` in the worktree briefly overwrote prod's Prisma client with one generated from my new schema. I caught it immediately, confirmed `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma` was untouched, and regenerated against prod's real schema to restore it — verified `nxeon-web.service` is `active` and serving 200s. Worth a permanent fix (e.g. an isolated Prisma output path for worktrees) but out of scope here.

### `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts` — action signatures
All five match the spec exactly, including formData field names (`gameType`, `gameMode`, `label`):
- `listFreeMinecraftWorlds(): Promise<{ok:true; worlds:{gameType; label; lastPlayedAt; isActive}[]} | {ok:false; error}>`
- `switchFreeMinecraftGameType(prev, formData): Promise<{error?: string}>`
- `applyFreeMinecraftGameMode(prev, formData): Promise<{error?: string}>`
- `renameFreeMinecraftWorld(prev, formData): Promise<{error?: string}>`
- `deleteFreeMinecraftWorld(prev, formData): Promise<{error?: string}>`

I did **not** delete `FREEMC_PRESETS` or the `preset` column as the brief suggested. Three excluded files (`components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, `ModsTab.tsx`, `FreeMinecraftTabContent.tsx`) read `row.preset` / `FREEMC_PRESETS[...]` directly and I'm barred from editing them — dropping either would fail the build, which is also mandatory. ### Schema diff (`prisma/schema.prisma`)
- New `FreeMinecraftWorld` model: `id, serverId→server, gameType, label?, lastPlayedAt?, createdAt`, `@@unique([serverId, gameType])`.

`grep -rn "\.preset\b" lib/ components/ app/` was re-run after every edit. 1. Two containers, same `/data` volume, `LEVEL=testmodeA` then `LEVEL=testmodeB`: both folder sets coexisted untouched.
2. Paper+IridiumSkyblock with `LEVEL=skyblock`: base world correctly became `skyblock`/`skyblock_nether`/`skyblock_the_end` (confirmed via `ServerLevel[skyblock]` in logs) — **but** IridiumSkyblock's own dimensions stay hardcoded as `iridiumskyblock`/`iridiumskyblock_nether`/`iridiumskyblock_the_end` regardless of `LEVEL`.
